key_insight: Instead of searching existing text for clues about a model’s internal signals, Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) generate text designed to activate a chosen residual stream direction. This moves interpretation beyond examples available in a fixed corpus.
problem_solved: Corpus-based searches can only reveal activating examples that already exist in the dataset, potentially limiting how well researchers can interpret a model’s internal directions.
method: Supply a direction from a subject language model’s residual stream to a MAEM.
Use the MAEM to generate text exemplars intended to strongly activate that direction.
Optimize for cosine alignment between the supplied direction and the subject model’s resulting activation, as described in the provided abstract excerpt.
impact: MAEMs could help practitioners explore internal model representations without relying solely on corpus searches. Generated exemplars offer interpretability clues, but do not by themselves establish a direction’s complete meaning or causal role.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: residual stream direction → MAEM → generated text → subject-model activation.
Side-by-side comparison: searching a fixed corpus versus generating targeted exemplars.
Vector diagram illustrating cosine alignment between a target direction and a text-induced activation.
Magnifying-glass icon over example text to represent inspection of internal signals.
paper_title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
paper_authors: Celeste De Schamphelaere, Juan J. Vazquez, Ari Spiesberger, Tomáš Gavenčiak, Gavin Leech
